subject: Commit category boundary change + seller fireside invite
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit category boundary change + seller fireside invite

Team —

Quick background and ask: finance has been flagging several late-stage slips in July/Aug that materially moved our net new ARR forecast. After a short analysis with Ella in FP&A, we propose tightening the definition for "Commit" to reduce noise in the weekly forecast. The proposed changes are in the attached commit-definition-v2.pdf and summarized below.

Proposed definition (high level):
- Commit: Signed purchase order OR explicit C-level verbal approval + procurement kickoff scheduled.
- Best Case: Strong commercial alignment (verbal buyer approval) and active procurement but no signed PO; >60% probability signals from PSC checklist.
- Pipeline (later stages): All remaining opportunities with active engagement but lacking either procurement readiness or exec confirmation.

Why this change? 
- Small set of large deals slipping has a disproportionate impact on our commit accuracy. Requirement for procurement kickoff or PO reduces optimistic commits that never enter legal/procurement.
- This is intentionally conservative for forecast integrity; we'll surface exceptions via a short weekly "Commit Exceptions" ledger for the CRO to review.

Immediate asks:
1) Read the attached doc and leave inline comments on the Google Doc by EOD Friday: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB_example_commit_definitions
2) Update any deals you currently have in Commit that would no longer meet the definition and move to Best Case before next Friday's forecast. Mark them with the tag "PROJ-commit-check" in HubSpot (hubspot:deal/9821).
3) Join a 30-minute seller fireside on Friday Aug 20 at 10:00am PT where Pete (FP&A) and I will run through the checklist, exception handling, and Q&A. Slides attached for seller-facing talking points.

I've attached a short FAQ and a checklist (commit-definition-v2.pdf). Jonas, can you coordinate a short note for the regional sellers so they have a one-slide handout? Marissa — I'd like your recommended exception workflow. Vivek — we'll need CS/Account Ops alignment for renewal-handled deals.

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik Iyer
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit category boundary change + seller fireside invite

Thanks Karthik — read the doc and left 3 inline comments. A couple quick notes: 

- Retroactive deals: do we apply this to deals that were already reported as Commit prior to Aug 1? My view: no retroactive reclassification for closed-loop integrity, but we should run a one-time review for big pipe (>$100k ARR) to see where the slippage came from.
- Exception workflow suggestion: central "Commit Exceptions" sheet owned by Revenue Ops; sellers request an exception with two required fields: reason + supporting evidence (email thread or signed term sheet). Ops will validate against checklist and put on CRO weekly agenda.
- Training ask: can we record the Aug 20 session and create a 10-min on-demand summary for late joiners? If Jonas is building the handout, I'll throw together a quick checklist card for reps.

Attaching seller-fireside-slides.pptx as a draft. I highlighted the suggested talking points and one new objection-handling script around procurement timelines.

Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Commit category boundary change + seller fireside invite

Hi Sara — looping you in briefly because your procurement team's cadence is similar to several of our customers and we want to be transparent about how we will classify Commit vs Best Case going forward.

Short summary for your team: Commit now requires either (a) signed PO, or (b) C-level verbal approval plus a scheduled procurement kickoff. This only affects internal forecasting; it does not change the progress of our implementation. If your team expects a delay in procurement kickoff scheduling, please let us know — we will mark the opportunity as Best Case until kickoff is scheduled.

Sara, if acceptable, could you confirm the expected procurement timeline for RDW-9821? If the procurement kickoff is scheduled, we'll keep it in Commit per the new policy.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit category boundary change + seller fireside invite — next steps

Appreciate the quick turns. Final notes and assignments: 

- No retroactive reclassification for deals closed as Commit prior to Aug 1, unless FP&A flags a material variance >$100k ARR. Marissa to own the one-time review for >$100k deals (due Aug 27).
- Revenue Ops will publish the "Commit Exceptions" Google Sheet. Jonas to add current exception candidates (5 deals) by Monday.
- Training: fireside Friday 10:00am PT is confirmed; session will be recorded and a 10-min summary clip + one-page checklist will be produced the following week. Jonas — please confirm you can run the seller-facing part; Marissa will handle exception workflow slides.

Deliverables and owners: 
- Commit Exceptions sheet (Revenue Ops): Vivek — link to be shared by Mon Aug 22.
- >$100k retro review (Marissa): due Fri Aug 27.
- Seller fireside recording + 10-min summary (Growth Enablement): Jonas to run session; Ops to publish recording by Aug 26.

If no objections, I'll push the new Commit definition to the forecast rules on Monday and ask FP&A to include a small footnote in the weekly deck for 3 weeks calling out the policy change.

Thanks all —
Karthik
